title: Texas' Most Unique High School Football Stadiums - NewsBreak
text:
By Buddy Logan ,
5 hours ago
It’s a fact. The best high school football movies are always set in Texas. I don’t make the rules; it’s just a fact.
In the great state of Texas, during the fall, Friday nights are revered, and our young men are forged in football pads and exalted to legends in their hometowns.
Texas’s Most Unique High School Football Stadiums Texas regularly has more players in the NFL than any other state . Last year, we had 211 Texans playing for the National Football League. California was in a distant second place with a paltry 151. And we won’t even mention that around 10 million more people live in the Golden State than here.
Download the KNUE Mobile App Now Mistakenly sitting next to the opposing teams’ parents (which happened at my high school because we only had bleachers on one side) is not something you’ll have to worry about at these Texas high school stadiums. Most here are massive, and we are sure to keep opposing fans separated.
Texas is home to many impressive high school football stadiums, and the price tags on the 10 biggest range from a staggering $38 million to an even more staggering $80 million .
Interestingly, the stadium with the largest capacity only comes in at No. 4 on the list. And the stadium taking the top spot holds fewer fans than all but the stadium in the 10th spot. If you’d like a complete rundown of the most expensive stadiums in Texas, click here .
Any ISD in Texas can drop millions on a brand-new stadium, though. How about we look at some of The Most Unique High School Football Stadiums in Texas? And let us know if there are any that need to be added to the list.
Texas' Most Unique High School Football Stadiums SBLive looked at some of the most unique high school stadiums that Texas has to offer, "from the Panhandle to the Rio Grande Valley." SBLive 8. Eagle Stadium, Allen "Since its debut in 2012, Eagle Stadium has had the attention of high school football fans across the Lone Star State — and the country. With a cost of $60 million and a capacity of 18,000..." READ MORE . SBLive 7. Mustang Bowl, Sweetwater "Easily one of the most unique stadiums in Texas, the Mustang Bowl is a full seating bowl dug into the ground with a capacity of 7,500... Brimming with history, it is well worth a trip out west to experience." READ MORE . SBLive 6. Alamo Stadium, San Antonio "... Opened in 1940, this venue has one of the most distinct designs with its quarry stone exterior, flat bowl-style seating and tile murals." READ MORE . SBLive 5. Heroes Stadium, San Antonio "... Built on the former Longhorn Quarry, it is a beautiful facility that includes a track and tremendous sightlines for fans." READ MORE . SBLive 4. Ratliff Stadium, Odessa "Ratliff Stadium seats 19,000 fans... Prominently featured in the book and movie, "Friday Night Lights," about Permian High School football..." READ MORE . SBLive 3. Lobo Stadium, Longview "Since it opened in 1977, Lobo Stadium had the look and feel of a college football stadium long before the modern marvels came onto the scene." READ MORE . SBLive 2. The Pfield, Pflugerville "... The Pfield also has pop culture significance as the home of the fictional Dillon Panthers on the hit TV series, "Friday Night Lights." READ MORE . SBLive 1.
